close_reason: Updated SetErrorType doc to honestly acknowledge the mail-variant carve-out (10 RFC 8620 base + 13 RFC 8621 mail-specific + Custom) and explicitly forbid further extension-specific variants. New-extension authors are pointed at SetErrorType::custom. Filed JMAP-wlip.35 (labelled 'human', P3) for the architectural decision on whether to move the 13 mail variants out of the foundation at the next workspace major bump — that decision requires explicit input on workspace versioning roadmap and is too invasive for an autonomous code change.
description:
Path: crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:181-232. SetErrorType is declared in the foundation `jmap-server` crate but the variant list mixes RFC 8620 base variants (Forbidden, OverQuota, NotFound, etc.) with 13 RFC 8621 mail-specific variants:
  MailboxHasChild, MailboxHasEmail, TooManyKeywords, TooManyMailboxes, BlobNotFound,
  ForbiddenFrom, InvalidEmail, TooManyRecipients, NoRecipients, InvalidRecipients,
  ForbiddenMailFrom, ForbiddenToSend, CannotUnsend

The doc at backend.rs:176-178 says:
  "Extension crates define their own error strings via SetErrorType::custom rather than adding variants here. This keeps the base crate stable as new JMAP extension crates (calendar, contacts, etc.) are added."

But the implementation already violates that policy by including mail variants in the foundation. New extensions (Calendars, Tasks, Contacts, FileNode, Sharing, Metadata, Chat, future drafts) have to use SetErrorType::custom("rateLimited") or similar — they don't get named variants — while mail gets a privileged position. This is asymmetric and the asymmetry is shipping in the foundation crate.

Concrete consequences for callers:
1. Symmetry violation. A user comparing `SetErrorType::custom("forbidden") == SetErrorType::Forbidden` discovers they are not equal (one is Custom(String), the other is the Forbidden variant). The same comparison `SetErrorType::custom("invalidRecipients") == SetErrorType::InvalidRecipients` likewise fails. Mail-extension consumers can pattern-match on `SetErrorType::InvalidRecipients` cleanly; chat/calendar consumers writing the equivalent custom-string comparison cannot.
2. Stability hostage. If RFC 8621 ever ships a normative change to one of these error type names (e.g., renames `forbiddenFrom` to `invalidFromAddress`), the foundation crate has to cut a major version. The foundation should NOT be the layer that breaks when an extension spec revises.
3. Doc-vs-code disagreement. New contributors read the doc, decide "I'll add a CalendarFullyBooked variant for jmap-calendars-server", attempt to add it to SetErrorType, and get pushback citing the doc. The asymmetry is invisible.

Right shape (forward-compat-only): leave the mail variants where they are (removing is breaking) but update the doc comment to be honest about the existing state — e.g. "The variant set below preserves RFC 8621 mail error strings for back-compat reasons; new extension errors MUST use SetErrorType::custom — only this base crate's bd:JMAP-X bead can add named variants." File a separate bead to decide whether the mail variants should be eventually moved to jmap-mail-types in a future major.

Right shape (clean): mail variants move to jmap-mail-types and the foundation SetErrorType keeps only RFC 8620 §5.3 variants. This is a breaking change, requires a workspace-wide major bump, and per the canonical-templates rule cascades to every extension *-server crate. Worth doing IFF the workspace is already planning a major bump.

Either way the current shape — silently-shipped asymmetry — is the worst option.
title: SetErrorType in foundation jmap-server carries 13 RFC 8621 mail-specific variants — contradicts the doc-stated extension-via-Custom policy and locks foundation's stability to mail-extension churn
